title: Proposal to Undo Privatisation of Postal Service
what_it_is: Proposal to Undo Privatisation of Postal Service

sections.label: SingPost mail delivery standards
sections.summary: SingPost must deliver 99% of CBD and 98% of non-CBD local basic letters by the next working day, and mis-delivery feedback fell from 279 in 2013 to 50 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: SingPost's Basic Mail Services are subjected to one of the most stringent Quality of Service standards in the world − SingPost must deliver 99% of local basic letters destined for the Central Business District (CBD), and 98% for those destined for non-CBD areas, by the next working day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since 2014, SingPost has invested in new machines and enhanced its staff training programme to improve mail sorting and delivery of letters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As a result of these measures, the incidents of feedback received by SingPost concerning mis-deliveries of local basic letters have dropped from 279 in 2013 to 50 in 2016.

sections.label: Licensed letter delivery companies
sections.summary: Four companies, including SingPost, are licensed to deliver letters in Singapore, and postal rates remain among the lowest among economies such as the United States, Hong Kong and Norway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Today, four companies, including SingPost, have been licensed to deliver letters in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Our postal rates continue to be among the lowest among economies, such as the United States, Hong Kong and Norway.

sections.label: Postal market liberalisation and feedback
sections.summary: The rationale for liberalising the postal market remains relevant, deprivatisation is not believed to necessarily improve outcomes, and feedback on misdelivered or missing letters sent to IMDA will be looked into seriously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The rationale behind our decision to liberalise the postal market still remains relevant today, and we have no reason to believe that deprivatisation will necessarily result in better outcomes and service quality for the postal sector in general.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Over the last few months, I have been receiving feedback from residents that letters were delivered to the wrong address or they are expecting letters but never received them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: If it is sent to IMDA, we will look into it seriously because, as I said earlier, we hold SingPost to the quality standards as part of the licensee agreement.
